candidate.attacker: An authenticated organization owner using the exposed Supabase/PostgREST interface
counterevidence: Server API routes perform ownership and site checks before normal application writes.
Those checks do not protect direct authenticated Supabase writes using the public client configuration.
No live database grant or migration-state probe was performed.
candidate.impact: Cross-tenant referential poisoning can corrupt confirmation, sharing, improvement, education, and audit relationships and can produce misleading tenant-scoped records.
candidate.recommended_remediation: After approval, add composite unique keys and composite foreign keys incorporating organization_id and, where required, site_id. Reconcile existing inconsistent rows first and tighten RLS checks to validate every related object.
candidate.source_to_sink_explanation: The schema stores organization_id alongside independently referenced site_id, workpack_id, worker_id, share_session_id, and improvement_id values. Foreign keys verify existence but not matching organization ownership. RLS policies authorize rows solely through their organization_id, allowing an owner to submit a row under their organization while referencing an object from another tenant.
supporting_source_evidence: workers, workpacks, and education_records reference sites, workpacks, or workers by ID without composite organization foreign keys.
Commercial tables repeat organization_id while independently referencing workpacks, sessions, workers, and improvements.
Commercial RLS WITH CHECK clauses validate only that the submitted organization_id belongs to auth.uid().
candidate.title: Related tenant objects are not bound to a consistent organization tuple
candidate.violated_security_invariant: Every site, workpack, worker, share session, confirmation, improvement, and photo relationship must belong to the same organization.

Generated database types expose the approval fields in both Insert and Update.
candidate.title: Workpack improvement approval metadata is client-forgeable

candidate.recommended_remediation: Make organization_id non-null for tenant records and remove the null wildcard. If platform records are required, isolate them in a separate table or authorize them through an explicit operator-role predicate.
candidate.source_to_sink_explanation: dispatch_logs permits organization_id to be null. supporting_source_evidence: organization_id is nullable.
The policy uses organization_id IS NULL as an unconditional authorization alternative for both existing and new rows.
The policy is FOR ALL rather than read-only.

candidate.attacker: An authenticated organization owner able to send concurrent worker-save requests
counterevidence: Sequential requests with an existing different-site row are rejected with WORKER_SITE_TRANSFER_REQUIRED.
The issue requires overlapping requests during the check-to-upsert interval.
candidate.impact: A worker can be silently reassigned, causing records, dispatch targeting, and training history to be associated with the wrong site.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Implement an atomic database function using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT with a site-equality predicate, or lock the worker identity row and reject any different-site update within the same transaction.
candidate.source_to_sink_explanation: The POST route first queries workers for conflicting site bindings and later performs an upsert on organization_id,external_key. Concurrent requests targeting different sites can both observe no conflicting row before either upsert commits; the later upsert then overwrites site_id.
supporting_source_evidence: The conflict check and upsert are separate database operations.
The unique constraint is organization_id,external_key, so the upsert updates the existing row rather than rejecting a different site.
No database predicate or transaction binds the checked site through the write.
candidate.title: Concurrent worker creation can silently transfer a worker between sites
candidate.violated_security_invariant: A worker already associated with one site must not be moved to another site without the explicit transfer workflow.

candidate.attacker: An authenticated user issuing concurrent first-use requests
counterevidence: Once a canonical row exists, ordinary sequential calls select and reuse it.
The condition requires concurrent initialization or deliberate overlapping requests.
candidate.impact: Tenant state can split across duplicate organizations or sites, producing inconsistent visibility, orphaned operational records, and authorization confusion.
candidate.recommended_remediation: After reconciling duplicates, add the intended unique constraints and move organization/site provisioning into one transactional function using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT.
candidate.source_to_sink_explanation: ensureWorkspaceContext selects the first organization for an owner and inserts when none exists, then separately selects and inserts a named site. The schema has no uniqueness constraint on organizations.owner_id or sites(organization_id,name), so concurrent first-use requests can each insert a sibling row.
supporting_source_evidence: Provisioning uses select-then-insert twice without a transaction.
organizations has no owner_id uniqueness constraint.
sites has no organization_id,name uniqueness constraint.
candidate.title: Initial workspace provisioning can create duplicate organizations or sites
candidate.violated_security_invariant: A user must have one canonical initial organization and one canonical site for a given organization and site name.

candidate.attacker: An authenticated site owner sending concurrent token-issuance requests
counterevidence: Authentication and site ownership are checked.
Sequential requests are rejected when the active count has reached the limit.
Issued tokens have bounded lifetime metadata.
candidate.impact: A site can exceed the intended active-token quota, expanding credential exposure and administrative load.
candidate.recommended_remediation: Issue tokens through a transactional per-site database function that locks a quota/site row, recounts eligible tokens, and conditionally inserts in the same transaction.
candidate.source_to_sink_explanation: The token endpoint counts active tokens, checks the limit in application code, then performs a separate insert. Multiple concurrent requests can all observe a count below the cap and each insert a new token.
supporting_source_evidence: The count and insert are distinct Supabase requests.
No transaction, advisory lock, quota row, or database enforcement connects them.
candidate.title: MCP active-token limit is vulnerable to concurrent issuance
candidate.violated_security_invariant: The configured maximum number of active MCP tokens per site must be enforced atomically.
